title: DR1 searches the notification list on three terms — keyword or notification number, commodity code or name, and consignee or importer; the frontend's one search box matches the reference number only.

finding.frontend: The filter panel holds one text box labelled "Keyword or reference" and a Search button. The label promises a keyword search but the value is passed straight through as a reference-number match — the controller reads request.query.referenceNumber and hands it to the list read under that name (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/controller.js:54-59), which puts it on the notifications request as referenceNumber (src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/read.js:30-34). A user who types a commodity or a consignee's name gets no results.
finding.prototype: The sidebar's first collapsible section, "Search by", holds three separate labelled boxes: "Keyword or notification number", "Commodity code or name" and "Consignee/Importer" (app/views/dashboard.html:87-132). The three are markup only — they sit outside every form on the page, and getDashboardViewModel never reads a keyword, commodity or consignee value and never filters the list (app/routes.js:7138-7255). DR1 states which three things a user should be able to search on; it does not demonstrate any of them working.
finding.difference: Replace the single box with the three DR1 asks for, and make each one search what its label promises. The frontend already carries the reference-number search, so the keyword box is the existing one relabelled and widened from an exact reference match to a keyword match. Commodity and consignee are new: the notifications endpoint accepts page, sort and reference number and nothing else (src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/read.js:26-34), so both need a search parameter added to the contract, and consignee matching needs the search to reach the party names the address book holds rather than the notification record alone.
finding.falsifiedBy: Typing a commodity name or a consignee name into the frontend's search box and getting the matching notification back.
finding.correction: Sound, and the inertness claim it rests on is verified independently. The rendered DR1 dashboard contains exactly one form element and it holds only the sort select, so all ten sidebar inputs — keyword, commodity, consignee, status, three date-range radios, start date and end date — sit outside every form and no browser submit can carry any of them. getDashboardViewModel never reads query.keyword, query.commodity or query.consignee, and the only thing that changes which notifications appear is the tab default; nothing else filters. One thing to record so a later reader does not think the finding wrong: the function does read one free-text key, query.search, and returns it as search, but no control on the root dashboard is named search and the root view never renders it, so the claim that DR1 never reads a keyword value stands. The frontend side is exact: controller.js:54-59 reads request.query.referenceNumber and hands it to the list read under that name, and read.js:30-34 puts it on the notifications request as referenceNumber and adds nothing else. The three labels are quoted correctly and are visible in evidence/prototype@491b3926/page/dr1-dashboard-filters-open.png.
